senses.gloss:
1. Menā in a few passages of the Rigveda denotes ‘woman.’ The word is also used in the sense of the ‘female’ of an animal, either mare or cow.
Foot notes Rv. i. 62, 7; 95, 6; ii. 39, 2.
Rv. i. 121, 2.
x. 111, 3.
Cf. Pischel, Indische Studien, 2, 316, 317.

2. Menā or menakā is mentioned in the Rigveda and in the Brāhmaṇas as the daughter, or perhaps wife, of vṛṣaṇaśva. The meaning of the legend connected with her is quite unknown. Cf. maināka or Mainaga.
Foot notes This is the ordinary form of the name.
So Ṣaḍviṃśa brāhmaṇa, i. 1, where the masculine form Mena is the epithet of vṛṣaṇaśva.
Rv. i. 51, 13, where Sāyaṇa tells the legend from the Śāṭyāyanaka. Cf. Oertel, Journal of the American Oriental Society, 16, ccxl.
Ṣaḍviṃśa brāhmaṇa, i. 1; Śatapatha brāhmaṇa, iii. 3, 4, 18; taittirīya Āraṇyaka, i. 12, 3; Lāṭyāyana śrauta sūtra. i. 3, 17.
Cf. Eggeling, Sacred Books of the East, 16, 81, n.
